.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Lowered the dew points through Saturday afternoon with NBM being
too high each afternoon. Otherwise, no significant changes were
made to the forecast. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Dry conditions and seasonable temperatures through early 
  next week, with frost possible this weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry conditions and seasonable temperatures through 
early next week, with frost possible this weekend.

Surface high pressure remains to the north through Saturday with
dry conditions and seasonal temperatures expected to continue.
High temperatures today will be in the 60s for most with only
highest elevations staying in the 50s. Tonight, low temperatures
will be in the upper 30s to 40s. For Friday and Saturday,
surface high pressure extends southward from Canada with dry
cold fronts bringing in cooler air. High temperatures stay in
the 50s to low 60s while overnight lows plummet into the 30s for
most. The exception will be east of the I-95 corridor where low
temperatures stay in the low 40s. Frost is possible Friday and
Saturday night. 

High pressure will continue to build southward into the region 
Sunday through Tuesday. Dry conditions and seasonable 
temperatures expected each day with light north to east winds. A
backdoor cold front could try to push into the region Tuesday 
into Tuesday night, but will have very little to no moisture 
with it to produce any precipitation. A surge of cooler 
temperatures will follow behind the front for the day on 
Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION /07Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
North winds continue today with terminals near the metros
gusting 15 to 20 knots this afternoon. Winds become light
overnight before shifting to northeast on Friday. Winds blow 5
to 10 knots on Friday before becoming light and variable
overnight. On Saturday, winds shift to easterly, remaining light
throughout the day. VFR conditions are expected each day. 

VFR conditions Sunday through Monday night. Winds light and variable 
through the period.

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisory conditions continue across the Chesapeake
Bay and lower tidal potomac through tonight before diminishing
Friday morning as subtropical storm Josephine tracks NE away
from the mid-atlantic. Friday afternoon through Saturday, light
winds are expected across the waters. The exception will be in 
the southern portions of the Chesapeake Bay where wind gusts 
near advisory criteria. 

No marine hazards expected Sunday through Monday night. Winds light 
and variable through the period.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Elevated tide levels are expected through the weekend as we approach 
the Full Moon on October 26, along with being in King Tide season 
(though we are already past the highest astronomical tides that were 
at the beginning of October). Sensitive locations are forecast to 
reach Action Stage during most of the high tide cycles this week, 
with locations at Annapolis, Solomons Island, Dahlgren, Straits Point, 
and Alexandria reaching minor tidal flooding. The presence of 
northerly winds is likely to keep tidal flooding within Minor flood 
stage.
